accounting_and_acceptance.hard_caps: Preserve 24 model calls, max_attempts=1, zero prompt/completion/request price, 36 outer MCP calls, one exclusive admission, empty isolated cache, original Entrez pacing, and all existing internal search/selection/return bounds. Two HTTP retransmissions are the only added bounded retrieval allowance.
accounting_and_acceptance.history: Study versions 1-3 and their stop/retry policies stay immutable and unscored. v4 must be preregistered as a new method version before admission, explicitly replacing only the new study's retrieval stop policy with this bounded recovery policy.
accounting_and_acceptance.science: Keep the six fixed positive/control pairs, matched shared-first-search design, prompts/model settings, exact target-PMID coverage metric, no-loss/control/unrelated-paper/provenance requirements, and all original scientific thresholds unchanged. Score only if all required pairs and blind labels are complete. Report recovered transient errors as operational reliability evidence; never describe the run as transport-error-free or erase them from the trace. A failed/exhausted request still makes the study incomplete, not a negative scientific result.
accounting_and_acceptance.trace: Add a bounded recovered_transient_attempts array with one row per failed physical Entrez attempt: study/run/build/process, operation, per-operation attempt ordinal, HTTP status, Retry-After value, wait applied, and final outcome. Count retries separately from existing method/rung counters; do not store query text, credentials, or full request URLs. Hidden Biopython retries remain max_tries=1. Keep unresolved fetch_errors and incomplete_fetch_count for exhausted failures only; a successful retry must still remain visible as a recovered transient event.

alternatives_rejected.batching: NCBI documents History/EFetch batching for large jobs, but this run retrieves at most nine selected records per call and the maintained client has no batch helper. Implementing one would create a broader retrieval/parser/cache change and would not recover ESearch errors. The independent 101-record source audit batch is not evidence of a maintained production-pilot batch path.
alternatives_rejected.live_pre_admission_canary: Adds an unscored retrieval/cache footprint and cannot predict whether later requests will fail; it consumes external request budget without testing the actual failure boundary.
alternatives_rejected.slower_pacing: No observed evidence shows 2.5 requests/s violated NCBI's 3/s cap; extra delay cannot resolve a 502 and cannot guarantee against shared-IP 429s. The v3 attempt already fell within NCBI's off-peak window, so merely scheduling off-peak is not a material recovery method.

confidence: High that the bounded policy is technically implementable at existing seams and materially differs from v1-v3. Medium that it is campaign-acceptable without an explicit distinction between unchanged scientific thresholds and the new operational transport policy; the preregistration must make that distinction explicit.

existing_seams: All maintained ESearch/EFetch/ELink calls use entrez_call; calling it again naturally re-enters the existing pacer.
Metadata is cached only after _fetch_paper_details succeeds, so an in-seam EFetch retry occurs before metadata cache publication.

No maintained bulk-metadata helper exists. Current selected IDs use per-paper EFetch/ELink with up to three concurrent metadata tasks; a batch rewrite would add parsing, ordering, and PMC-link/cache semantics and would not address ESearch 502.
observed: v2 stopped on upstream PubMed HTTP 502 during ESearch; v3 stopped on upstream metadata HTTP 429. Both admissions are consumed and remain terminal/inconclusive; v1 is also consumed and incomplete.

The maintained process-wide pacer in engine/mcp_server/entrez_rate_limit.py spaces no-key requests at 0.4 seconds (2.5/s), below NCBI's 3/s guidance. The failures do not establish a local pacing defect.

Pilot tracing pins Biopython max_tries=1/sleep=0. Its 1.86 source retries HTTP 429 and other HTTP errors internally without the project's synchronized pacer; that hidden retry path must remain disabled.

The runner currently rejects any fetch_errors/incomplete rows and requires the 1/0 Entrez policy. v4 therefore needs its own explicit registration/trace validator; do not alter v1-v3 receipts or validator semantics.

limitations: This proposal does not predict whether an upstream transient will recover; a persistent or third transient still consumes the one-shot study and leaves its scientific metric incomplete.

If the campaign owner requires a literal zero-transient-error operational gate in addition to the unchanged scientific criteria, a recovered transient can never satisfy that gate; retain the logged event and report that outcome separately rather than calling it error-free.
This design does not establish that current Entrez pacing is defective and does not justify changing product-wide retry behavior.

engine/mcp_server/pubmed_pilot_trace.py: initialize and emit the new v4 attempt trace while retaining max_tries=1
references/external/sakana/novelty_result_conditioned_pilot.py: v4-only registration and trace validation; keep v1-v3 branches unchanged
minimal_change_and_test_boundary.offline_test_cases: Use fake HTTPError/clock/sleep only: 429 and 502 retry exactly once; Retry-After seconds/date is honored; absent header waits 15s; >60s stops; the second transient failure does not loop; study-wide retry cap stops; other 4xx/5xx are terminal; exact kwargs/cache behavior are unchanged; every attempt is traced; each retry goes through the process pacer. No external provider test is needed to verify this policy boundary.

recommendation: For a separately registered v4 prospective comparison, add a narrowly bounded, retrieval-only retry policy at the existing Entrez request seam. This is the only reviewed option that directly addresses the observed 502/429 interruptions without changing the scientific inputs, model route, query semantics, or outcome thresholds.

title: M12 fourth-study retrieval recovery design audit

v4_operational_policy.bounds: At most one retry for any single logical Entrez call and at most two retries total for the entire admitted study. No model retry, outer MCP replay, resume, restart, alternate search, or repeated retry after the one retry fails.
v4_operational_policy.delay: Honor a valid Retry-After value exactly when it is at most 60 seconds. With no usable header, wait 15 seconds. If Retry-After requests more than 60 seconds, stop without retry rather than retrying early. Every retry then reserves a fresh slot through the existing 0.4-second process pacer.
v4_operational_policy.eligible_requests: Idempotent maintained Entrez ESearch, EFetch, and ELink reads only; reuse the exact original operation and parameters.
v4_operational_policy.otherwise: All other HTTP statuses, parse errors, process/provenance errors, model/admission/price failures, and exhausted retry budget remain terminal for the admitted study. No key, model, query, cache, tool, fixture, prompt, or request-cost setting changes.

required_corrections: Study-wide retry allowance must not reset for each MCP trace
Preserve and validate recovered, exhausted and physical-attempt accounting in v4 results
Keep default-off activation and all v1-v3 output/validation unchanged
Commit actual fresh bank, protocol, source hashes and verify isolation/admission before scientific requests
